abstract.t: This document specifies the NetPerfMeter Protocol (NPMP), a network performance benchmarking and metering protocol designed for comparative evaluations across multiple Transport Layer protocols, including TCP, MPTCP, UDP, SCTP, DCCP, and QUIC. NPMP is decoupled into a reliable Control Channel (NPMP-CONTROL) for testbed orchestration, scenario parameter negotiation, and scalar/vector result retrieval, and one or more Data Channels (NPMP-DATA) conveying synthetic application workloads with fine-grained QoS metric collection (throughput, delay, jitter, and packet loss). This document describes the protocol architecture, state transitions, packet formats, IANA-registered identifiers (PPIDs, Service Codes, and ALPN strings), reference implementations, and simulation models in the OMNeT++ INET Framework.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Evaluating and comparing the performance of Transport Layer protocols under realistic operating conditions requires an application protocol capable of generating identical, highly configurable, and reproducible traffic workloads across fundamentally different transport services. Existing network evaluation utilities typically specialize in single-stream bulk data transfers (such as TTCP or early versions of Iperf and Netperf), or focus exclusively on isolated protocols like TCP or UDP without providing concurrent multi-stream, multi-protocol, or multi-path testing facilities.

The NetPerfMeter Protocol (NPMP) provides a unified protocol architecture explicitly designed for multi-protocol transport benchmarking. As defined in the NetPerfMeter tool-chain (see and ), NPMP decouples the control signaling (NPMP-CONTROL) from the measurement data transmission (NPMP-DATA). This separation enables test orchestrators to systematically evaluate both single-path and multi-path protocols (such as Concurrent Multipath Transfer for SCTP (CMT-SCTP) and Multipath TCP (MPTCP)) while preventing control signaling from distorting measured transport dynamics.

NPMP supports bidirectional saturated flows (bulk transfers), non-saturated flows (configurable constant or randomized frame rates and sizes to mimic interactive and multimedia traffic), on/off traffic patterns, and partial reliability / unordered delivery options.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: This document uses the following terms:

ul.li: Active Node: The endpoint initiating the measurement session (client), responsible for configuring scenario parameters, commanding measurement start/stop, and downloading remote measurement results.
Passive Node: The endpoint awaiting connections (server), which receives scenario configurations, binds listener sockets, generates requested inbound traffic, and records statistics.

Control Channel (NPMP-CONTROL): The reliable signaling association used to orchestrate the measurement lifecycle, exchange flow configurations, synchronize start/stop events, and transfer result files.
Data Channel (NPMP-DATA): The communication association(s) established over the transport protocol under test (TCP, MPTCP, UDP, SCTP, DCCP, or QUIC) carrying timestamped payload data.
Frame: The application-layer data unit produced by the traffic generator at a specified or randomized rate and size.
Message: The transport-layer data packet into which application frames are segmented if their size exceeds the Maximum Message Size.
Flow: A configured communication relation characterized by unique flow and stream identifiers, a transport protocol, and directional traffic parameters.
Stream: A subchannel or stream within a multi-stream association (e.g., SCTP stream or QUIC unidirectional stream).

section.name: Dual-Channel Architecture
section.t: The fundamental design principle of NPMP is the separation of control plane coordination from data plane execution:
section.artwork: +---------------------+ +---------------------+ | Active Node | | Passive Node | | (Client) | | (Server) | +---------------------+ +---------------------+ | NPMP-CONTROL Client |<=== Control Channel ===>| NPMP-CONTROL Server | | | (SCTP or TCP) | | | NPMP-DATA Sender/ |<==== Data Channel(s) ==>| NPMP-DATA Sender/ | | Receiver | (TCP/MPTCP/UDP/ | Receiver | +---------------------+ SCTP/DCCP/QUIC) +---------------------+
section.t: The Control Channel operates over a reliable connection-oriented transport protocol (by default SCTP using PPID 36, or TCP). It remains active for the entire duration of the session to ensure reliable delivery of management commands. The Data Channel encompasses all data flows generated according to the traffic specifications, utilizing any supported transport protocol:

ul.li: TCP: Transmission Control Protocol .
MPTCP: Multipath TCP .
UDP: User Datagram Protocol .
SCTP: Stream Control Transmission Protocol , including Partial Reliability (PR-SCTP) .
DCCP: Datagram Congestion Control Protocol , including CCID 2 and CCID 3 .
QUIC: QUIC Transport Protocol over TLS .

section.name: Measurement Session Lifecycle
section.t: A measurement session proceeds through four distinct phases:

ol.li: Configuration Phase: The Active Node connects to the Passive Node via NPMP-CONTROL and defines one or more flows using NETPERFMETER_ADD_FLOW messages, each acknowledged with NETPERFMETER_ACKNOWLEDGE.

Association and Identification Phase: The Active Node establishes the data transport connection(s) to the Passive Node's data port(s). Over each data connection, it transmits a NETPERFMETER_IDENTIFY_FLOW message containing a unique 64-bit magic number, Measurement ID, Flow ID, and Stream ID. The Passive Node binds the new socket/stream to the configured flow state and confirms via NETPERFMETER_ACKNOWLEDGE on the Control Channel.

Measurement Phase: The Active Node issues a NETPERFMETER_START message. Upon acknowledgment, both nodes launch transmission threads, generating timestamped NETPERFMETER_DATA messages according to the traffic specs, and logging vector/scalar statistics.

Termination and Retrieval Phase: When the runtime expires or an abort is signaled, the Active Node issues NETPERFMETER_STOP. After stopping local flows, both endpoints close data streams. The Active Node then requests the recorded passive-side scalar and vector files using chunked NETPERFMETER_RESULTS messages, concludes by removing flows via NETPERFMETER_REMOVE_FLOW, and closes the session.

section.name: Protocol Message Formats
section.t: All NPMP messages are binary-encoded. Multi-byte integer fields MUST be transmitted in network byte order (big-endian), unless explicitly stated otherwise.

section.name: Common Message Header
section.t: Every NPMP message starts with a 4-octet header:

li.t: Type (8 bits): Identifies the message type:

ul.li: 0x01: NETPERFMETER_ACKNOWLEDGE
0x02: NETPERFMETER_ADD_FLOW
0x03: NETPERFMETER_REMOVE_FLOW
0x04: NETPERFMETER_IDENTIFY_FLOW
0x05: NETPERFMETER_DATA
0x06: NETPERFMETER_START
0x07: NETPERFMETER_STOP
0x08: NETPERFMETER_RESULTS
Flags (8 bits): Type-specific flags (default 0x00).
Length (16 bits): Total length of the message in octets, including the header and any variable payload.

section.name: NETPERFMETER_ACKNOWLEDGE Message
section.t: Transmitted over the Control Channel to acknowledge preceding requests.

ul.li: FlowID (32 bits): Flow identifier referenced by the acknowledgment.
MeasurementID (64 bits): Unique identifier of the measurement run.
StreamID (16 bits): Stream index within the flow (e.g. SCTP stream).
Padding (16 bits): Reserved; MUST be set to 0.
Status (32 bits): Result status: 0 denotes success (Okay); 1 denotes an error condition (Error).

section.name: NETPERFMETER_ADD_FLOW Message
section.t: Configures a new flow on the peer. It specifies transport options, buffer sizes, congestion control, and random parameter arrays for frame rate, frame size, and on/off events.
Notable flags and fields include:

ul.li: Flags: Bit 0: Debug mode; Bit 1: NoDelay (disable Nagle); Bit 2: Repeat on/off events.
Protocol: Transport protocol number (IPPROTO_TCP, IPPROTO_UDP, IPPROTO_SCTP, IPPROTO_DCCP, IPPROTO_MPTCP, or IPPROTO_QUIC). Note: encoded in little-endian format for historical compatibility.
OrderedMode: Scaled 32-bit probability [0.0, 1.0] for ordered delivery.
ReliableMode: Scaled 32-bit probability [0.0, 1.0] for reliable delivery.
RetransmissionTrials: Number of trials, or timeout in milliseconds if Bit 31 is set.
FrameRate / FrameSize: 4 network 64-bit floating point numbers defining distribution parameters.
FrameRateRng / FrameSizeRng: Random number generator identifier (Constant=0, Uniform=1, Exponential=2, Pareto=3, Normal=4, TruncNormal=5).
CMT: Concurrent Multipath Transfer mode (0=Off, 1=CMT, 2=CMT/RPv1, 3=CMT/RPv2, 4=MPTCP-like).
CCID: DCCP Congestion Control Identifier (e.g. 2 or 3).
OnOffEvents: Count of trailing NetPerfMeterOnOffEvent records (each 36 octets).
NDiffPorts, PathMgr, Scheduler: Obsolete configuration fields retained for wire compatibility with legacy Linux kernel MPTCP implementations.

section.name: NETPERFMETER_IDENTIFY_FLOW Message
section.t: Transmitted over newly established data channels to correlate the underlying transport socket/stream with its configured flow definition:
The 64-bit MagicNumber (0x4bcdf3aa303c6774) ensures that unintentional or malformed data connections are detected and rejected prior to association.

section.name: NETPERFMETER_DATA Message
section.t: Conveys synthetic payload over active Data Channels:

ul.li: Flags: Bit 0 (NPMDF_FRAME_BEGIN) indicates frame start; Bit 1 (NPMDF_FRAME_END) indicates frame termination.
FrameID (32 bits): Incrementing frame identifier.
SeqNumber (64 bits): Packet sequence number for loss tracking.
ByteSeqNumber (64 bits): Cumulative transmitted byte count.
TimeStamp (64 bits): Transmission microsecond timestamp for latency and jitter calculation.
Payload: Variable bytes filled with deterministic test patterns (e.g., repeating byte sequences 30..127).

section.name: Start, Stop, and Results Messages
section.t: The remaining control messages supervise measurement execution:

ul.li: NETPERFMETER_START (Type 0x06, 16 octets): Commands the passive node to commence traffic transmission and local vector/scalar logging for the specified MeasurementID. Flags specify file compression and format.
NETPERFMETER_STOP (Type 0x07, 16 octets): Commands termination of data transmission and finalization of measurement statistics.

NETPERFMETER_RESULTS (Type 0x08, 4 octets header + up to 1400 octets data): Transfers captured vector and scalar log files from the passive node to the active node in sequential chunks. Bit 0 of Flags (NPMRF_EOF) denotes the final chunk of a downloaded file.
NETPERFMETER_REMOVE_FLOW (Type 0x03, 18 octets): Removes flow state and triggers download of the corresponding flow's vector file.

section.name: Traffic Generation and Quality of Service Metrics
Traffic Models
section.t: NetPerfMeter generates traffic as discrete frames. A flow is either saturated (frame rate set to 0, sending as fast as the transport layer permits) or non-saturated (governed by frame rate and frame size distributions). Supported distributions include:

ul.li: Constant: Deterministic frame rate and size.
Uniform: Distributed within [min, max].
Exponential: Negative exponential distribution for Poisson arrivals.
Pareto: Heavy-tailed distribution to model bursty Internet traffic.
Normal / Truncated Normal: Gaussian distribution.

section.name: Open Source Software Implementation
section.t: The reference software implementation of NetPerfMeter is written in C++ and released under the GNU General Public License (GPLv3). It runs on Linux, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, Solaris, GNU Hurd, and macOS.

section.name: OMNeT++ INET Framework Simulation Model
section.t: NetPerfMeter is integrated into the well-known INET Framework for the OMNeT++ discrete-event network simulator as the module:

This simulation model, documented in , implements the same flow specification parameters, random traffic distributions, and metrics logging as the real-world tool. This ensures that scenarios simulated in OMNeT++ can be replicated identically in physical testbed environments such as NorNet.

section.name: Wireshark Protocol Dissector
section.t: The Wireshark network protocol analyzer provides built-in dissectors for the NetPerfMeter Protocol in the dissector module packet-netperfmeter.c. It decodes both NPMP-CONTROL and NPMP-DATA messages across all underlying transport protocols.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: NPMP is a measurement tool intended for performance evaluation in research, laboratory, and operational testbed environments. Unauthenticated control channels could allow malicious actors to instruct endpoints to establish high-volume denial-of-service traffic streams.

When operating across public or untrusted networks, the Control Channel SHOULD be protected by network-layer security (IPsec) or transport-layer security. QUIC data channels MUST enforce mutual TLS certificate authentication as specified in .
